Upstream only applies `cds--tabs--full-width` when its `lg`-breakpoint media query also matches (`distributeWidth = fullWidth && contained && isLg && ...`); Ember's `showFullWidthClass` never checks the viewport. The fixture was generated in jsdom, where generate.mjs's `matchMedia` stub never matches (there is no real viewport), so upstream records the narrow-viewport answer - a real, if small, Ember gap: below `lg` Ember still distributes tab widths where upstream doesn't.

Same out-of-subtree id-reference harness limitation as the tabs' `aria-controls` entries above, from the panel's side: its `aria-labelledby` points back at the tab button, outside the picked panel subtree, so the raw generated ids are compared (`ccs-<useId>-tab-0` vs. `<guidFor>-tab-0`) - same `<base>-tab-<index>` scheme on both sides.

Ember's yielded `TabPane` renders `tabindex="0"` on its panel; the pinned `@carbon/react`'s `TabPanel` renders none. Left as-is: it only makes the panel itself focusable, which the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern recommends when a panel has no focusable content of its own, and removing it would silently change keyboard behaviour for existing consumers - a real, deliberate-looking divergence rather than a markup slip.
